title: Run the machine reuse gate on every development branch push

scope.subject: Repository-wide push-time reuse enforcement without duplicating expensive browser CI

research_summary: Extend the existing GitHub Actions and repository-local Node reuse gate so every branch push receives authoritative push-range policy validation, while keeping production build and Playwright work limited to main pushes, pull requests, and explicit manual validation.

sources.finding: GitHub Actions push branch filters can match every branch with a glob while keeping tags out when only branches are configured; job-level conditions can then limit downstream expensive jobs.
OPA is a mature general-purpose policy-as-code engine suitable for CI/CD, but introducing it here would duplicate the repository-local Node policy engine already used by the machine reuse gate.
Backstage provides a broad centralized software-governance/catalog platform intended for much larger organizational surfaces than one repository push-policy gap.
Git hooks provide local lifecycle enforcement but are client-side and cannot serve as the authoritative control for changes pushed from GitHub-only or other remote development environments.

search_ladder.conclusion: Backstage can model broad software governance, but deploying a full developer portal is disproportionate to enforcing one repository's push-time reuse policy.
OPA/Conftest can express the policy generically, but adopting a second policy language and runtime would duplicate the existing Node gate for no meaningful coverage gain.

GitHub Actions already receives branch push events and the existing Node gate already understands commit ranges, so widening the workflow trigger is the smallest authoritative remote enforcement change.
Git hooks remain useful fast local feedback, but cannot enforce pushes created from remote agents or GitHub-only editing and therefore remain supplemental.

candidates.name: Existing Node reuse gate on every GitHub branch push
candidates.source: GitHub Actions push event plus repository-local Node gate
candidates.license: Project code plus GitHub hosted CI
candidates.reason: Reuses the current authoritative gate and its push-range diff support, closes the branch-push bypass, and adds only a lightweight hosted job instead of another policy runtime.

candidates.name: OPA / Conftest push policy
candidates.reason: Capable but would add Rego and another policy runtime while the existing Node gate already implements the exact approval, provenance, and changed-file semantics required here.

candidates.name: Backstage governance platform
candidates.reason: Its organization-scale catalog and portal capabilities are much broader than this repository trigger gap and would impose a service-sized operational surface.

candidates.name: Local Git hooks only
candidates.reason: Retain local hooks for fast feedback, but they cannot be authoritative for remote agents or GitHub-side edits and therefore cannot close the branch-push enforcement gap alone.

coverage_matrix.capability: Authoritative enforcement on every ordinary development branch push
coverage_matrix.decision: Use the existing Node gate in GitHub Actions on all branch pushes so remote and local development paths receive the same commit-range policy check.

coverage_matrix.capability: Avoid expensive duplicate build and browser work for branch pushes that already receive pull-request validation
coverage_matrix.decision: Run the lightweight reuse-gate job for every branch push, but condition production build and Playwright jobs to main pushes, pull requests, or manual validation.

coverage_matrix.capability: Preserve the existing approval/provenance policy implementation
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep one policy authority by reusing the current Node gate rather than translating the approval and Git-provenance semantics into a second engine.

decision.rationale: Widen the existing GitHub Actions push trigger to all branches and reuse the current commit-range-aware Node gate. Keep costly build and Playwright jobs conditional so ordinary branch pushes gain machine enforcement without multiplying browser CI cost.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: Backstage is a broader full solution, but its catalog, portal, deployment, and operational requirements are disproportionate to a single-repository push enforcement gap.
OPA is a broader policy framework, but translating the already-working task approval and Git provenance semantics would duplicate policy ownership without increasing enforcement coverage.

decision.fallback: If GitHub Actions push-run cost becomes material, split the machine gate into a dedicated lightweight workflow with path filters while preserving all-branch push coverage for protected implementation files.
